text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - UK shares ended a nervous election-day session on Thursday with a closing record but by the slimmest of margins as many investors stayed away ahead of the ballot result which is due in the early hours of Friday morning. The FTSE 100 index closed 9.0 points higher to a new peak of 4,445.0, only 0.7 points above the previous all-time high of 4,444.3, reached on March 11.
FRANKFURT - The German stocks market was closed on Thursday for a market holiday. On Wednesday the DAX-30 index of leading German shares ended the session up 54.88 points at 3,438.07.
PARIS - The French stocks were closed on Thursday for a market holiday. On Wednesday the CAC-40 index closed up 36.60 points at 2639.46.
ZURICH - Swiss stocks were closed on Thursday for a market holiday. On Wednesday the Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 23.70 points to 3,094.65.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended modestly higher on Thursday supported by buying of some major issues after early gains on buying of blue chips were eroded by profit-taking, brokers said. They said gains in recent sessions were too rapid and the indices needed to take a breather. The 225-share Nikkei average closed 124.21 points higher at 19,275.33.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks rose steeply for the second day in a row on Thursday, closing above the 13,000-point level for the first time since mid-March as gains on Wall Street propelled prices higher, brokers said. The blue-chip Hang Seng Index soared 117.48 points, to finish at 13,020.78.

SYDNEY - Local indecision and persistent nervousness over Wall Street's behaviour pushed the Australian share market just lower by the close on Thursday. The All Ordinaries index lost 2.6 points to 2,485.4. Continued scepticism over Wall Street's rebound, with key economic data still to come in the U.S., compounded by stronger than expected local wages data saw the market endure a day of choppy, rangebound trade with little real direction.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares were closed on Thursday fir a market holiday. On Wednesday the overall index ended up 23.5 points at 7,130.5, the industrial index gained 41.5 points to 8,494.3 points and the gold index dropped 18.2 points to fresh four-year low of 1,187.0 points.
